key_insight: Laser post-treatment improved wear resistance of Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings from both spray methods, with greater hardness gains for detonation-sprayed coatings.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to improve wear performance on coated AISI 321 stainless steel, but stiffness changes depend on the deposition method.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying (DS) and gas-flame spraying (GFS).
Compare microstructure and phases before and after laser treatment using SEM, EDS and XRD.
Evaluate hardness, elastic modulus and dry-sliding performance using indentation and ball-on-disk testing.
evidence_signal: Wear rates decreased by approximately 24% for DS and 39% for GFS; hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV for DS and from 1096.2 to 1121.3 HV for GFS.
watch_item: GFS elastic modulus decreased from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa after laser treatment, so improved wear resistance should not be assumed to imply improved stiffness.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
